quotes.text: Learn how to save Naver Pay to charge your customers later.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Learn how to save Naver Pay to charge your customers later.
Your customer must authorize you to use their NICEPAY account for future payments through Stripe Checkout.
The `off_session` value must also be set to true if the customer isn’t in a checkout flow for this PaymentIntent.
Recurring payments must be made with `capture_method: "automatic"`. Manual capture isn’t supported.

findings: November repeats the purpose and links the same two variants that May included in full (new raw lines 5-14, old raw lines 4-14 and 141-153). Capture format and link presentation changed without a demonstrated behavioral or availability change.

May requires permission and a record of the customer's written agreement. For off-session use, document authority, frequency/timing, how the amount is determined and cancellation policy for subscriptions, and charge only under agreed terms (old raw lines 29-40 and 208-219). Bind the payment method to a customer-configured Accounts v2 Account or a Customers v1 Customer. May says Connect GA, public preview otherwise and preview-version pin when participating (old raw lines 42-86 and 155-199).

May Checkout sets up future use through hosted `mode: 'setup'` and NICEPAY authorization. The sample method list contains `card` and `naver_pay`. The separate billing guide uses `subscription` mode in its own Checkout variant and does not change this setup-mode example (old raw lines 88-139, wiki/sources/source-stripe-subscriptions-naver-pay.md:32-40).

May Direct API creates a bound `naver_pay` SetupIntent server-side for later use, with `usage` selectable as `on_session` or `off_session` in prose and the latter in samples. The browser calls `confirmNaverPaySetup` with the SetupIntent secret, return URL and the shown online acceptance with `infer_from_client`. A different server PaymentIntent path attempts payment while saving with `setup_future_usage: 'off_session'`, a return URL and mandate data if creating a mandate. The latter examples contain non-authoritative NGN values (old raw lines 221-261, 293-380 and 442-518).

May later creates and confirms a new KRW PaymentIntent using the same saved PaymentMethod ID and the matching Account or Customer. Off-session context and recurring capture restriction are separate. Server detachment deactivates the method for reuse and sends `mandate.updated` and `payment_method.detached`; separate test paragraphs describe hosted setup authorize/fail choices and PaymentIntent test outcomes, without establishing setup status enums or live results (old raw lines 137-139, 520-572).

source_assessments.reason: The index is navigation-only. Independently correct the baseline scope of recurring capture, identity/consent fields and historical conflicting examples.

answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/naver-pay/set-up-future-payments identifies saving Naver Pay for later charges and lists Checkout and Direct API. It provides navigation (new raw lines 5-14). The May 8 guide documents prior opt-in and recorded written terms and binds the saved method to a Customers v1 Customer or customer-configured Accounts v2 Account. It describes Accounts v2 as generally available for Connect and a version-qualified public preview for other Stripe users (old raw lines 29-56 and old raw lines 155-167). Its hosted Checkout setup-mode flow requires the customer to authorize future NICEPAY use. The Direct API SetupIntent is created on the server, its SetupIntent secret is passed to the browser, and the browser calls confirmNaverPaySetup with a return URL and online acceptance. A separate server PaymentIntent can attempt a payment while saving with setup_future_usage off_session. To charge later, use the same saved PaymentMethod ID on a new PaymentIntent with the corresponding customer identity. Set off_session when the customer is outside the checkout flow. The May recurring rule requires automatic capture. Setup, authorization or browser return does not establish successful payment. The guide reports that server detachment deactivates reusable methods and sends mandate.updated and payment_method.detached (old raw lines 88-139, old raw lines 221-261, old raw lines 330-440 and old raw lines 442-572). source-stripe-naver-pay-set-up-future-payments.md captures the May paths and currency conflict but overstates the no-manual-capture rule for all off-session payments.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/naver-pay/set-up-future-payments, new raw lines 5-14 retain the purpose and replace May's Checkout and Direct API variant bodies with links. Operational claims about mandates, account representation, one- and two-step payment flows, setup usage, SDK example, recurring capture and detach remain dated to May 8, 2026 (old raw lines 29-56, old raw lines 208-261, old raw lines 330-380 and old raw lines 442-572). In source-stripe-naver-pay-set-up-future-payments.md and the reciprocal Korea concept route, preserve the mismatch between the two historical NGN charge-and-save examples and documented KRW, and distinguish recurring automatic capture from the independent off_session condition. The old SetupIntent prose borrows a PaymentIntent secret gloss despite showing a SetupIntent secret. The optional manual redirect sample uses a PaymentIntent without the save fields, so its requires_action and browser return describe a payment action and cannot establish future-use setup or payment success (old raw lines 259-297, old raw lines 358-440 and old raw lines 449-564). Preserve the Checkout sandbox setup authorize/fail choice separately from the historical PaymentIntent sandbox outcome. No variant implementation or current availability was established by the index.
